messages:
maria: Heads-up: canary for 'phase-split + ephemeral-queue' shows an 8–12% p99 tail increase on g4 nodes after we split prefill/decode. Attached a flamegraph and p95/p99 numbers. Anyone else seeing this?

ash: Saw it. p50 stable, p95 +2–4ms, p99 +20–35ms. My quick look points at KV cold misses on the decode path — decode workers aren't seeing warmed KV because prefill writes to an ephemeral queue and priming events don't cross over.

kevin: Interesting. Can you paste the flamegraph link & the canary config?

maria: link: https://internal/perf/5409876543/flame.svg
Config snippet:
```yaml
queue_policy: phase_aware_ephemeral
token_budget_target: 64
kv_priming: disabled
prefill_workers: 4
decode_workers: 8
```
We turned kv_priming off to reduce coupling — looks like that backfired for decode-heavy tails.

julia: :eyes: Traces confirm it — decode workers spike on `kv.fetch` during first decode tokens; lots of cold misses.

perf-bot: perf-bot: Canary run 5409876543 — baseline vs canary diff:
p50: 0.2%
p95: +3ms
p99: +28ms
QPS: same
KV hit-rate: 98.7% -> 94.3% (first 10s of session)

ash: Hypothesis: separating queues prevents prefix KV priming since prefill completes on the prefill queue and doesn't forward priming hints to decode. Options:
- shared priming inlet (bridge)
- on-decode warmup handshake (decode pulls prefix fingerprint and fetches KV inline)
- adaptive token_budget that forces inline micro-prefill for short requests

kevin: We tried a bridge in sim env and saw ~12% p99 improvement. Bridge adds small cross-queue handshake latency though. Can we do lightweight in-proc priming to avoid the extra hop?

maria: Bench notes: enabled `kv_priming: bridge` and ran 10k mixed requests:
p99 dropped to baseline +5%
cpu overhead +1.6%
Tradeoff looks reasonable for now.

julia: Also observed a kernel-selection mismatch: decode batch shapes prefer tensor-core kernels but prefill batches were selecting different kernels. When queues are split, the kernel selector loses the global batch-shape view and ends up mapping suboptimal kernels for decode.

ash: Exactly — kernel selection is per-worker-pool today. We need a global kernel-affinity hint broker so prefill and decode pools can share profiling/choice stats.

kevin: Action items:
1) Re-enable kv_priming bridge on canary (maria)
2) Prototype kernel-affinity broker to aggregate kernel choices (ash + eng-infra)
3) Add 'decode token_budget adaptive' as opt-in flag for rollout (julia)
I'll create perf-task cards for these.

maria: I'll flip bridge on in the next canary (5409900000) and post numbers.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary 5409900000 started on g4-cluster-us-east-1

ash: Additional tweak: add probabilistic sampling to shed expensive prefill flow for short requests. Proposed sampling rule:
```json
{
  "sampling": {"seed": 0.05, "short_req_threshold_tokens": 16, "inline_prefill": true}
}
```
This forces tiny inline prefill for 5% of short requests and avoids heavy priming churn for the long tail.

julia: Good. Also add trace points for `kernel.selector.choice` and `kv.fetch.latency` (prefill/decode labels) so we can validate improvements.

kevin: Can we target rollout tomorrow EOD? Goal: regressions <6% p99 vs baseline.

maria: sg. Will report back by EOD with canary numbers and flamegraphs. :thumbsup:
